newsitem.title: VATICAN: Two Italian priests get visa to work in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Two Italian priests get visa to work in Cuba.

text.p: Cuba has granted two Italian priests permission to work in the country following Pope John Paul's meeting with communist leader Fidel Castro, a Roman Catholic news service said on Friday.
SIR, a news agency that serves Catholic weeklies in Italy, said two priests from northern Italy had been granted visas, usually difficult for foreign priests to obtain.
It said Cuba had granted the visas a few days before Castro held his first meeting with the Pope at the Vatican on Tuesday.
The Pope accepted the veteran revolutionary's invitation to visit the island next year.
SIR said a visit to Cuba earlier this month by Vatican "foreign minister" Archbishop Jean-Louis Tauran had also helped expedite the visa request, made more than a year ago.
One of the priests, Giulio Battistella, said he expected a tough time on the island and was not certain the Pope would actually make it to Cuba.

"If there is dialogue at the top of the Church and the Cuban state, the grass roots situation has not changed. The bureaucracy and state apparatus still try in every way possible to hinder the work of missionaries and the Church," he said.
"And I am not fooling myself over an eventual visit by the Pope to Cuba: even if Castro has invited him, many on the island still oppose him," Battistella added.
